en: The *Bilu jing* (Sūtra on the Crown Prince Bilu) Spoken by the Buddha;
the *Sengyou lu* states it was a "Miraculous Sūtra from Guanzhong" and is now appended to the Qin Records.
Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park. The deva...

The Prince, named Piluo, flew down from heaven and descended to where the Buddha was. He prostrated himself with his five limbs touching the ground, bowed his head at the Buddha’s feet, and then stood with palms joined, asking the Buddha:
"All people in the world seek clothing and food, the seven treasures and various pleasures, official rank, and kingdoms. Is there perhaps a 'jewel-like practice' that seeks out such people?"
The World-Honored One praised him, saying:
"How great is this question!
There are indeed lands, treasures, and various desires that people seek and pursue."
P’i-lo spoke again:
“Regarding those who seek a person through the practice of their cherished wishes, what is the meaning of this?
The World-Honored One then said:
“There are two paths in all: practicing good brings blessing, while practicing evil brings calamity. Calamity and blessing follow a person just as a shadow follows a form.
Pilinda said: “Excellent, excellent!”
It is indeed as the Buddha taught.
Formerly, in a previous life, I lived in the world as a king. Reflecting on the impermanence of life, I desired to practice giving. The ministers assembled, and the king said:
"I wish to have a great drum made, whose sound shall resound for a hundred li; is there anyone capable of doing this?"
The ministers all replied, "We are incapable of doing so.
There was one minister named Kuang-shang, who was always loyal to his sovereign and compassionate toward the people; he stepped forward and said:
"I am able to do it, but I require the necessary funds," he said.
The king replied,
"Excellent!"
He immediately opened the treasury and entrusted it to him.
Thereupon, he transported the treasures to the gate of the royal palace and beat the drums to proclaim:

"Today, the King, a benevolent and compassionate ruler, bestows boundless mercy; desiring to relieve the poverty of the common people and provide for the food and clothing of the practitioners of the Way."
"Should there be any who are destitute, let them all go to the palace gate.
Those in distress from the four states came bearing infants on their backs, supporting one another as they filled the roads to the kingdom;
looking up to heaven, they sighed and said, "The people who were at their wits' end shall now find life!"
After one year had passed, the king issued a decree, saying:
"Is the drum finished?
They replied: [as follows].
"It is finished," [the artisan] replied. The King asked,
"Why did you not hear its sound?"
The minister addressed him, saying:

"I pray that Your Majesty, the Enlightened King, will condescend to exert your holy body and come forth to visit within the realm, so that you may hear the sound of the Dharma drum, which resounds throughout the ten directions.
The king immediately prepared his carriage and went out through the kingdom.
The people were so numerous that they stood shoulder to shoulder, whereupon the King said, "Are the people many? They replied: [They were exceedingly many.]
“Your Majesty previously commanded your servant to have a great drum made that could be heard for a hundred li, desiring thereby to spread the sound of Your Majesty’s virtue to the four quarters.
Your servant reflects, however, that withered wood and dead bark cannot propagate the King’s virtuous reputation.”
The treasures received by your servant are used to provide clothing and food for śramaṇas and brahmins, thereby relieving the poverty of the people.
Upon the arrival of this proclamation, the neighboring states returned to receive its benefits, like hungry children longing for their compassionate mother.
The king asked the man,
"Where have you come from?
The man bowed his head to the ground and replied:
"Those who have come from a hundred li, those from two hundred li, and those from ten thousand li away," they all said,

"The Enlightened King has bestowed great bounty, and the four nations rejoice in his grace. Therefore, we have abandoned the lands where we were born to long for this nourishing moisture so as to sustain ourselves."
The King said: "Excellent!
I am captivated."
"The instability of the state is like an illness in the body; I treat it with medicine, and my ministers nourish it with congee.
The King said, "Let the common people have their desires fulfilled as they wish; do not trouble me with reports."
"After the king’s life ended, his spirit ascended to be born in the heavens as a Wondrous King of Heaven.

When his lifespan in heaven was exhausted, he descended to be born in the world with the rank of a Universal Monarch (Cakravartin). He traveled at will, flying through the air with the seven treasures, leading and followed by his retinue before and behind."
Now he has ascended once more to heaven as the Crown Prince of a celestial king.
The reason for this is that he personally upheld the precepts and rescued and aided sentient beings;
by revering the Buddha’s teachings and precepts, and rectifying his physical and mental conduct, there is none who does not obtain their blessings.
The Buddha told P’i-lo:
“When ordinary people perform actions, it is like a shadow following the body or an echo responding to a sound; there is nothing that does not receive its retribution.”
Vairocana was filled with joy, paid his respects, and departed.
This concludes the *Buddha-bhāṣita-vairocana-devaputra-sūtra*.
